title: HiddenKeywordSpellings
description: Issue #154. Five gates decide what a schema states by re-marshalling it and reading the keys, and marshalling drops two spellings: `enum` is tagged omitempty so "enum": [] leaves no key, and "const": null is held on a field tagged "-" because encoding/json cannot tell a null constant from an absent one. A schema stating only one of those read as a schema stating nothing, so each gate handed its position a type with no check on it. Every property here pairs the hidden spelling with the spelling that was always read -- `false` beside the empty enum, a string constant beside the null one -- and the two must now be answered alike. The accept row beside each rejection is the value the schema does admit; where a schema admits nothing at all, it is the document that leaves the property out.
